subject: Invitation to FLOC Networking Event - Connect and Collaborate!
content:
Dear UTA Organizations,

I hope this email finds you well.

The Freshman Leaders on Campus at UTA is excited to invite your organization to a unique Networking Event on October 1st, from 6-8pm at Carlisle Hall. This event aims to connect our members with various organizations (such as yourselves) across campus, fostering a collaborative environment and showcasing opportunities beyond individual groups.

We believe that cross-organizational networking is crucial for personal and professional growth. This event provides a platform four our members to engage with peers from different and similar fields, exchanging ideas, and discover new avenues for collaboration.

To maximize your organization’s exposure, we encourage you to bring flyers and set up a small table to promote your activities and opportunities. We are happy to assist with printing flyers if needed.

Given the short notice we understand the need for flexibility. We sincerely hope you will consider this valuable opportunity to connect, collaborate, and expand horizons. Please RSVP by Friday 9/26 so we can make the necessary arrangements.

We look forward to seeing you there!

Best regards,

Andrea Ponce
Vice President
Freshman Leaders on Campus (FLOC)
asp6148@mavs.uta.edu<mailto:asp6148@mavs.uta.edu>

P.S. If you have any questions please don’t hesitate to reach out to asp6148@mavs.uta.edu<mailto:asp6148@mavs.uta.edu> (my email) or aht0065@mavs.uta.edu<mailto:aht0065@mavs.uta.edu> (our president’s).

subject: Shake Smart Fundraiser
content:
Good afternoon!

I am reaching out for the idea of a potential fundraiser at the UT Arlington Shake Smart location; we admire your organization and would love to become more involved in helping all of our campus kitties! Below I have the guidelines we have set for fundraisers. Due to the high demand of fundraisers at our locations, we are only able to offer one-day fundraisers. Once you read through them, we will be able to move forward with planning a few more logistics.

Our fundraisers generally consist of a percentage of credit/debit sales, from participants from your organization, donated back to your org. Below I have outlined the guidelines for an event like this just so you have all the information that you need!

  *
10 % of credit card sales contributed from the fundraiser will be given back to your organization once the fundraising day has concluded in the form of a check. All customers must mention they are there for the fundraiser for their sale to count towards this percentage.
  *
All signage and marketing is to be done by the group hosting the fundraiser, Shake Smart is not responsible for either. Some ideas to get the word out could be to create a flyer or signage promoting the event, mention it in any university classes and to professors, have individuals get excited about the event at meetings, encourage family/friends to come support your cause, post on an Instagram page! You are responsible for whatever avenue of marketing you choose to use.
  *
In addition, we can not have affiliates of the organization standing outside Shake Smart or near the building entrance passing out fliers or catering to constituents who were already planning on visiting Shake Smart- a simple exploitation of the fundraising process that will not be allowed. I am sure this won’t be an issue with your organization but prefer to always clarify the parameters in advance. If you could please make sure this is communicated to all participants I would appreciate it!


Let me know if this is something you would be interested in doing and we can pick out a date for the fundraiser!

subject: Luciano: Request for Advice
content:
Good afternoon. My name is Luciano Martinez, and I’m sending you this
message primarily to ask for your advice on a situation I found myself
involving a stray cat and her babies taking refuge in my backyard. I became
aware of your group (UTA Campus Cat Coalition) from my younger brother who
attends UTA, and I want to put my trust in a group of cat enthusiasts run
by students over my city’s cat and animal resources.

For starters, I live in the 76112 area of Fort Worth, which is about a 15
minute drive away from the University of Texas at Arlington. Some time in
July, a pregnant stray cat was wandering in my backyard, and since I
already have a cat and cat food of my own, I fed her, and she pretty much
made my backyard her refuge. I always had the idea of wanting to catch her
and take her to an animal clinic, but she never let me get very close to
her. One day she just disappeared out of nowhere, then showed back up a few
days later with no belly. I thought maybe she had her kittens somewhere
else, but about a week later, her kittens started popping up in my backyard
and I found that she actually had them behind a shed that I never thought
to look behind. Long story short, I’ve been taking care of them, feeding
them three times a day, and they look mature enough that they’re walking
around and eating on their own. I attached a picture of the mama cat and
her five kittens to this message for reference. One thing to note is that
the picture of the mama cat is an older picture and her teats have shrunk
since then. These days, the mama cat and the babies let me get close enough
to somewhat pet them, but they’re still definitely shy around me.

My main point of this message is that I want to ask for your advice on what
I should do about this situation. I honestly can’t take care of the six
cats as I already have a cat of my own that possibly doesn’t get along with
the mama cat, and I frequently travel out of state. It’s not that I don’t
want them or am incapable of providing for them, but I honestly don’t think
they can live their best life in my backyard, especially with the colder,
darker months right around the corner. I think the mama cat has become
somewhat dependent on me feeding them as she stays sleeping on my back
porch for most of the day, and very rarely ever leaves to go hunting.

I know your organization primarily focuses around taking care of the cats
on UTA’s campus, so I don’t expect you specifically to take them. Ideally,
I wanted to ask if you knew of a trusted animal shelter or service that
could take them and help them find a proper forever home? If not, I have a
number of contacts provided by my city’s animal welfare services that I’d
like to share with you, but I want to wait for your reply before doing so
for the sake of simplicity.

Thank you very much in advance for taking the time to read and reply to me.
I appreciate whatever input you may have for me!

Hello!
My name is Siam Tungnung and I'm the Promotions Director for the Homecoming Committee. subject: Cat situation
content:
Good Morning,

I am a graduate student from UNLV that was flown in to Arlington to check
on elderly family who have had a stroke. Prior to her stroke, she was
caring for 8 cats that were rescue cats. Because of her stroke, she can no
longer care for these animals. They are box trained. All are
spayed/neutered. They have been living in doors with them. However, now
that she has had a stroke, she absolutely cannot care for these animals and
the state of the inside of her house says that they have not been able to
care for these animals for at least a month.

Your information was provided by cat enthusiasts that suggested that I
might reach out to you directly. If you could, in any way, take these cats,
they would go to a good home and be cared for. They are good cats, they've
just become so much more than a woman who cannot move can deal with. She's
now bed bound and these cats are creating a health issue for her because
she can't even get home health agencies to come and work with her as a
result of the state of the house.

I will be in town until Wednesday if you can reach me. 702-371-4377 is my
number. Their home is in Arlington off Fielder and Randoll Mill.

Regards,
Chris Percy
